title: SmoothQuant: Accurate Post-Training Quantization for LLMs
hook: Activations are hard to quantize; weights are easy. SmoothQuant shifts that difficulty from activations into weights with a simple rescaling, enabling clean 8-bit inference.
key_points: LLM activations contain large per-channel outliers that break naive quantization; weights do not.
Applies a per-channel scaling factor to smooth activation magnitudes, absorbing the inverse into the weight matrix.
The transformation is mathematically equivalent - no retraining or accuracy drop from the reparameterization itself.
Enables simultaneous W8A8 (8-bit weight and 8-bit activation) quantization with hardware-efficient INT8 kernels.
content_html: Xiao et al. identified a fundamental asymmetry in LLM quantization: weights have smooth, easy-to-quantize distributions, but activations contain large outlier values in specific channels that cause significant error when quantized to 8 bits. SmoothQuant exploits this asymmetry by migrating the quantization difficulty - mathematically - from activations onto weights before quantizing either.
extra_html:
How it works

For each channel, SmoothQuant divides the activation by a smoothing factor s and multiplies the corresponding weight row by the same s. The net effect on the linear layer's output is zero: it is a reparameterization, not an approximation. After smoothing, activations no longer have extreme outliers, so both activations and weights can be cleanly quantized to INT8. The smoothing factors are calibrated from a small dataset of real inputs.

Why it matters

Prior approaches either quantized only weights (leaving activations in FP16) or required expensive fine-tuning. SmoothQuant enables true W8A8 quantization - both multiplied operands in INT8 - which lets models run on commodity hardware with full use of INT8 matrix-multiply throughput. The authors report significant inference speedups on large models with minimal accuracy degradation. Full details are on arXiv.

related.title: LLM.int8(): 8-bit Inference for Transformers
related.hook: Big transformers usually run in 16-bit. LLM.int8() halves that to 8-bit integers without losing accuracy — by treating a few rare 'outlier' features with care.

related.title: GPTQ: Accurate Post-Training Quantization
related.hook: Already trained a giant LLM? GPTQ squeezes its weights down to 3–4 bits afterward — no retraining — with surprisingly little quality loss.

related.title: AWQ: Activation-Aware Weight Quantization
related.hook: Not all weights are equal - protect the 1% that matter most (flagged by activation magnitude) and quantize the rest to 4-bit with minimal quality loss.

related.title: Nunchaku: 4-bit Diffusion Inference in Diffusers
related.hook: Diffusion models hate 4-bit — activation outliers wreck image quality. SVDQuant peels the hardest weights into a tiny 16-bit low-rank branch, and Nunchaku now runs it inside Diffusers.
